In my final project, I will be looking at Reporters Without Boarder's World Freedom Index. The international nonprofit's mission is to defend the freedom of information by protecting journalists worldwide.

Every year, RSF publishes their World Freedom Press Freedom Index, a chart that tracks 180 countries' state of journalism. They look at factors including:

1. If journalists can make a livable wage (Economic factor)
2. If journalists are viewed as helpers of society (Social factor)
3. If journalists are supported by their governments (Political factor)
4. If journalists are safe reporting in their country (Safety factor)
5. If laws support the work of journalists (Legal factor)


All of these factors are added together to give a country an overall score that tells a country's state of journalism. These overall scores change from year to year as a country's state of journalism improves or worsens.

In my final project, I will see if Latin American countries experienced larger drops in overall scores from 2025 - 2026 compared to the rest of the world.

My first step is to install my libraries, upload the data and clean it.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
```

```{r}
freedom_index_2026 <- read_csv("data/rsf_data_2026.csv")
freedom_index_2026 <- freedom_index_2026 |> clean_names()
```

This is the first set of rsf data from 2026. Let's look at it.

```{r}
freedom_index_2026 |> tibble()
```

Great! Not only do we have each countries' score, but we also have each countries' ranking for each category.

Now, let's see the data from last year.

freedom_index_2025 <- read_csv("data/rsf_data_2025.csv")
